subject: Decision lanes, security boundary and questionnaire intake — next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Decision lanes, security boundary and questionnaire intake — next steps

Thanks for taking time earlier, Ethan — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from today’s demo)
- PayBot is evaluating Redwood for conversational customer support (api-facing) and a small batch-embedding pipeline for search.
- Decision criteria: latency under 200ms p50 for API flows, strong audit logs, and contractual DPA/Security obligations.
- Timeline: internal exec review in ~3 weeks; procurement expected after legal/security sign-off.

Immediate asks / owners
1) Economic buyer: please confirm who will sign (we understand CFO Sarah Li will be the decider). (Ethan)
2) Procurement lead & process: we need contact, PO timeline, and if you use a standard SOW or PO-first flow. (Ethan)
3) Security intake: we’re attaching our short questionnaire and a one-page summary — can you fill the questionnaire and confirm which systems will be in scope? (PayBot security)
4) Kickoff: propose a 30–45m security kickoff next week to walk questionnaire answers and scope boundaries. Suggested slots: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Attached: redwood-security-summary.pdf (one-pager), redwood-security-questionnaire.xlsx (short intake).

Next steps for Redwood
- I’ll schedule a security kickoff once you confirm attendees and a procurement contact.
- Marissa (CS) will prepare an initial deployment plan for a 4-week pilot if security clears the scope.

Thanks — Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: Sarah Li (CFO) will be the economic buyer and will sign the final agreement. I looped her on this thread.
- Procurement: procurement@paybot.io is the correct mailbox. Our standard flow is procurement review + PO; legal may request a few redlines but it’s usually PO-first for pilots under $50k.
- Timing: we can target procurement review the week of Aug 9 if security sign-off is done by end of July.

Security/scope notes: 
- We have an internal Security Team (led by Aaron Park) who will do the SOC/controls review. They will want a network diagram and a statement on how you persist logs/audit trails (retention period, location).
- Initial scope we expect: public API endpoints that will accept customer text; the batch embedding job that runs in our analytics account; and any admin UI that our support team will use.

I’ll ask Aaron to fill the questionnaire, but he’s out Wed–Thu this week — I expect a reply by Friday. If it helps, Sarah can attend a kickoff as well.

— Ethan

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Ethan — copied Aaron to bring him up to speed. A couple of clarifications and attachments that should help Aaron’s intake: 

- Attached: high-level network-diagram.png showing the two hosting modes we discussed (hosted API in Redwood-managed VPC; private-only onboarding via VPC peering for dedicated).
- Audit/logging: Redwood persists request/response metadata and system logs for 90 days by default in the hosted plan; dedicated/private options can extend retention and allow customer-managed KMS. We’ll provide a retention/export policy doc for procurement/legal if needed.

Can Aaron or your security lead confirm whether the following are in-scope for their review? Please reply with yes/no for each so we can scope the kickoff: 
- Customer-facing API (real-time inference) — expected in scope
- Batch embedding jobs (scheduled in your analytics account) — expected in scope
- Support/admin console (used by PayBot support agents) — likely in scope
- Data exports to third-party analytics (e.g., S3 sink) — clarify if those sinks are owned/managed by PayBot or third parties

Proposed kickoff times (adjust if needed):
- Tue, Jul 27 10:30–11:00 PT
- Wed, Jul 28 11:00–11:45 PT

If Aaron can’t make those windows, we’ll do an async review over the questionnaire and follow up with a shorter walkthrough.

Thanks — looking forward to Aaron’s input.

--
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — Soojin on security here, taking the lead from Redwood’s side for intake. Thanks, Lauren, for the materials — they’re helpful. Quick intake summary and next steps: 

What we need from PayBot for the kickoff (attach / answer before call or during):
- Completed redwood-security-questionnaire.xlsx (attached to initial mail).
- Network diagram that shows where Redwood-hosted endpoints will sit relative to PayBot VPCs (Lauren’s diagram is a great start).
- List of data flows: which attributes are PII, where embeddings are stored, and any third-party sinks.
- Primary security contacts (name + email + slack handle) — we’ll add them to the read-only evidence channel.

Preliminary systems-in-scope (please confirm):
- public customer-facing API (real-time inference)
- scheduled batch embedding pipeline (runs in PayBot analytics account)
- internal support/admin console (accessed by PayBot agents)
- logging/monitoring stack (whether Redwood-managed or PayBot-owned sinks)

Suggested agenda for the 30–45m kickoff:
1) Introductions & scope confirmation (5–7m)
2) Questionnaire walk-through & outstanding answers (10–15m)
3) Data flow & retention expectations (10m)
4) Next artifacts and timeline for evidence (5–10m)

We can run the kickoff Tue/Wed next week — Lauren, I’ll let you schedule (I’m available Tue 10:30–11:30 PT and Wed 11:00–12:00 PT).

Deliverables / owners from Redwood:
- Security intake owner: Soojin Lee (soojin_lee@redwood.com) — will coordinate evidence collection
- CS lead: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com) — pilot deployment plan
- AE owner: Lauren Bishop — procurement/legal coordination and exec alignment

If PayBot confirms the systems-in-scope and sends the completed questionnaire, we’ll aim to have a checklist of outstanding evidence within 48 hours of the kickoff.

Thanks — Soojin
